verses.ALMA 59:9: And now as Moroni had supposed that there should be men sent to the city of Nephihah, to the assistance of the people to maintain that city, and knowing that it was easier to keep the city from falling into the hands of the Lamanites than to retake it from them, he supposed that they would easily maintain that city.
verses.ALMA 60:30: Behold, I wait for assistance from you; and, except ye do administer unto our relief, behold, I come unto you, even in the land of Zarahemla, and smite you with the sword, insomuch that ye can have no more power to impede the progress of this people in the cause of our freedom.
verses.ALMA 61:8: They have got possession of the land, or the city, of Zarahemla; they have appointed a king over them, and he hath written unto the king of the Lamanites, in the which he hath joined an alliance with him; in the which alliance he hath agreed to maintain the city of Zarahemla, which maintenance he supposeth will enable the Lamanites to conquer the remainder of the land, and he shall be placed king over this people when they shall be conquered under the Lamanites.
verses.ALMA 61:18: And we will take possession of the city of Zarahemla, that we may obtain more food to send forth unto Lehi and Teancum; yea, we will go forth against them in the strength of the Lord, and we will put an end to this great iniquity.
verses.ALMA 62:3: And it came to pass that Moroni took a small number of men, according to the desire of Pahoran, and gave Lehi and Teancum command over the remainder of his army, and took his march towards the land of Gideon.
verses.ALMA 62:4: And he did raise the standard of liberty in whatsoever place he did enter, and gained whatsoever force he could in all his march towards the land of Gideon.
verses.ALMA 62:6: And thus, when Moroni had gathered together whatsoever men he could in all his march, he came to the land of Gideon; and uniting his forces with those of Pahoran they became exceedingly strong, even stronger than the men of Pachus, who was the king of those dissenters who had driven the freemen out of the land of Zarahemla and had taken possession of the land.
verses.ALMA 62:7: And it came to pass that Moroni and Pahoran went down with their armies into the land of Zarahemla, and went forth against the city, and did meet the men of Pachus, insomuch that they did come to battle.
verses.ALMA 62:14: And it came to pass that Moroni and Pahoran, leaving a large body of men in the land of Zarahemla, took their march with a large body of men towards the land of Nephihah, being determined to overthrow the Lamanites in that city.
verses.ALMA 62:18: And it came to pass that when they had sent them away they pursued their march towards the land of Nephihah. And it came to pass that when they had come to the city of Nephihah, they did pitch their tents in the plains of Nephihah, which is near the city of Nephihah.
verses.ALMA 62:25: And now when Moroni saw that they were fleeing before him, he did cause that his men should march forth against them, and slew many, and surrounded many others, and took them prisoners; and the remainder of them fled into the land of Moroni, which was in the borders by the seashore.
verses.ALMA 62:32: And it came to pass that Moroni and his army did pursue them from city to city, until they were met by Lehi and Teancum; and the Lamanites fled from Lehi and Teancum, even down upon the borders by the seashore, until they came to the land of Moroni.
verses.ALMA 62:34: And it came to pass that Moroni and Lehi and Teancum did encamp with their armies round about in the borders of the land of Moroni, insomuch that the Lamanites were encircled about in the borders by the wilderness on the south, and in the borders by the wilderness on the east.

tests.title: North/south and east/west statements form no loop
tests.summary: 22 north-south and 14 east-west statements were encoded. Treated as an ordering (A is north of B), they contain no cycle, with or without the weaker inferred ones, and one map satisfies all of them at once.
detail: The longest north-to-south chain the text supports is: Land Desolation > Land Bountiful > Zarahemla > Narrow strip of wilderness > Land / city of Nephi (Lehi-Nephi).
The longest west-to-east chain is: Gideon (valley & city) > River Sidon > Zarahemla > Wilderness of Hermounts.
Cycles found: north-south 0, east-west 0. I then built a layout from the constraints; it violates 0 of 20 north-south and 0 of 12 east-west rules (see the Map view).
Caveat: the text gives few absolute directions. Most are 'A is north of B' pairs, so this is a test for contradictions, not a proof that the map is unique.

tests.title: "Up" and "down" are used the same way throughout
tests.summary: Going toward Nephi is always 'up'; coming toward Zarahemla is always 'down'; leaving Nephi is 'down out of'. None of the matching verses I found reverses this.
detail: I searched every motion verb followed by 'up' or 'down' and a place name. Nephi and Zarahemla are the two best-attested endpoints, and the usage never flips.
One edge case: 3 Nephi 6:25 has a complaint 'came up unto the land of Zarahemla'. The origin is not stated, so it cannot be tested.
Mosiah 7:6 has Ammon go 'down into the land of Nephi' from the hill north of Shilom. That is a local descent into the city, so it fits.
Mormon 4:1 has the Nephites go 'up' out of Desolation toward the Lamanites, while Mormon 3:7 and 4:19 have the Lamanites 'come down' on Desolation. That pattern matches the rest: the south is higher.

rows.label: up Nephi: Travelling toward Nephi from Zarahemla (or from the north) is always 'up'
down Zarahemla: Travelling toward Zarahemla from the Lamanite lands (or from the west frontier) is always 'down'
down out of Nephi: Leaving Nephi is 'down'
up out of Zarahemla: Leaving Zarahemla for Nephi is 'up'
down Desolation: Lamanites attack Desolation from the south 'coming down'; Nephites leave it going 'up' (MORMON 4:1)
down Middoni: Middoni lies below Ishmael; Aaron/Ammon in Middoni are later reached 'up' from the Nephi side (ALMA 22:3)

tests.title: Every river-Sidon crossing puts places on the right bank
tests.summary: Zarahemla, Melek and Manti are on the west bank; Gideon, Hill Amnihu, Antionum, Nephihah and the 'south wilderness' crossed by Zoram are on the east. All crossing events agree with that.
detail: No place is assigned to both banks and no journey crosses the river the wrong way for its endpoints.

Alma 16:6-7 requires the Lamanite raiders to cross the Sidon from west to east on their way home beyond Manti. That fits Lamanite lands on the east side too (Alma 22:29, Alma 25:5), so it is a constraint, not a conflict.

tests.title: Two "sea to sea" lines: the strip in the south, the neck in the north
tests.summary: Alma 22 describes two different lines that each run from sea to sea. One is a narrow strip of wilderness south of Zarahemla; the other is the narrow neck at Bountiful and Desolation. The text keeps them apart, with Zarahemla and Bountiful between them.
detail: The strip is described as wilderness dividing the Lamanite kingdom from Zarahemla (Alma 22:27). The neck is described as a land bridge with sea on both sides (Alma 22:32, 50:34, Ether 10:20).

Terms are not mixed up: 'narrow strip' appears once, only for the southern wilderness (Alma 22:27), and 'neck', 'pass' and 'passage' appear only for the northern line (Alma 22:32, 50:34, 52:9, 63:5, Ether 10:20, Mormon 2:29, 3:5).
3 Nephi 3:23 names the stretch between them: Zarahemla, 'the land which was between', and then the line between Bountiful and Desolation.

tests.title: The east-coast cities fit one coastline
tests.summary: Moroni is the southernmost coastal city, Lehi is north of it, Mulek is the last before Bountiful, and Jershon and Antionum sit along the same coast. Everything lines up, but the text never says how Jershon relates to the six cities.
detail: Alma 51:26 lists six cities taken in one sweep, all 'on the east borders by the seashore'. Alma 51:28 then has the Lamanites reach 'the borders of the land Bountiful', so Bountiful is north of Mulek, and Alma 52:23 confirms it when Teancum retreats 'by the seashore, northward'.

Alma 27:22 says Jershon joins Bountiful from the south, and Alma 31:3 puts Antionum south of Jershon. Alma 50:13 puts Moroni at the south line. So the six cities and Jershon must share the same stretch of coast.
This is under-determined, not contradictory: the text does not say whether those cities are inside Jershon or a separate band.

tests.title: The neck: "a day and a half" or "a day"?
tests.summary: Alma 22:32 says the line between Bountiful and Desolation, east sea to west sea, is a day and a half's journey for a Nephite. Helaman 4:7 says the line the Nephites fortified from the west sea to the east is a day's journey for a Nephite.
detail: This is the only place where two numbers are given for what may be the same span.

Ways they could both be right: (1) it is not the same line, since Helaman 4:6-7 describes a defensive line inside Bountiful, to guard 'their north country', and the Alma line is the Bountiful-Desolation boundary; (2) 'a day's journey' is a round figure; (3) the two lines are at different places along a neck that narrows or widens.
Ways they conflict: if both are the Bountiful-Desolation line, 1.5 versus 1 is a 50% difference.
Verdict: not a hard contradiction, because the text never says they are the same line, but it is the one numeric tension in the geography.

tests.title: Nephi to Zarahemla: 20 days on one route, 40 when lost
tests.summary: Alma's people took 8 days to reach Helam and 12 more to reach Zarahemla, about 20 days. Ammon's party took 40 days, but the text says they did not know the way.
detail: Mosiah 23:3 gives eight days from the area of Mormon to Helam. Mosiah 24:25 gives twelve days from Helam to Zarahemla. A route of about 20 days therefore exists; it is not stated to be the shortest.
Mosiah 7:4-5 gives forty days for Ammon's sixteen men, with the explicit reason that they 'knew not the course'. A lost party taking twice as long as a guided one is no conflict.
Limhi's people and Mosiah's sons are both given only 'many days'. A 20-day route is a reasonable reading of 'many'.
No triangle test is possible: no pair of these places has two independent day counts.

tests.title: Melek to Ammonihah: three days north
tests.summary: Ammonihah is three days north of Melek, which is on the west bank. Nothing else in the text gives a competing distance or direction for it.
detail: Alma 8:3 puts Melek west of the Sidon, by the wilderness border. Alma 8:6 puts Ammonihah three days north. Alma 8:18 has Alma re-enter by the south side, which matches him returning from the south.
The Lamanites reach Ammonihah 'upon the wilderness side' (Alma 16:2) and later approach it again (Alma 49:1), which fits a city at the western edge.

tests.title: The Old World route has no reversals
tests.summary: Three days to a valley by a river, four days south-southeast to Shazer, many days on 'nearly the same course' to Nahom, then 'nearly eastward' to Bountiful. The headings never double back.
detail: The text's own stated headings are SSE, 'nearly the same course as in the beginning', and then 'nearly eastward'. Together they describe one turn, from south-southeast to east.
The whole overland trip is given as eight years in the wilderness (1 Nephi 17:4), which is a duration and not comparable to the day counts.
I did not map this onto any real-world place, as asked.

tests.title: Where did the Mulekites first land?
tests.summary: Alma 22:30 says the Jaredite bones land was 'the place of their first landing', and Helaman 6:10 says the Lord brought Mulek into the land north. Omni 1:16 says they crossed the waters 'into the land where Mosiah discovered them; and they had dwelt there from that time forth'.
detail: Alma and Helaman put the first landing in the north, near Desolation. Omni reads most naturally as landing and dwelling in Zarahemla.

A reconciliation exists: Omni 1:16 may compress an unrecorded migration south. Omni 1:21 also says Coriantumr 'was discovered by the people of Zarahemla', and Alma 22:30 says the bones land was 'discovered by the people of Zarahemla', so those people were in or near the north at some point.
Nothing in the text states the migration, so this is a gap, not a contradiction.

tests.title: The northern land is described the same way by five different writers
tests.summary: The land northward is a land of 'many waters', 'large bodies of water' and 'many rivers', with cement houses because timber is scarce, from Mosiah through Mormon.
detail: Limhi's scouts (Mosiah 8:8) describe a land among many waters. Alma 50:29 calls the land northward 'covered with large bodies of water'. Helaman 3:4 says the migrants reached 'large bodies of water and many rivers'. Mormon 6:4 puts Cumorah in 'a land of many waters, rivers, and fountains'.
Helaman 3:5-11 explains the timber and cement detail in the same land, and Helaman 3:10 says timber was shipped north, which fits a land reachable by sea.

tests.title: The southern wilderness is a hunting ground in both Jaredite and Nephite accounts
tests.summary: Ether 9 and 10 have flocks fleeing south from serpents and the Jaredites keeping the land southward 'for a wilderness, to get game'. Alma 22:31 describes Bountiful as a wilderness full of wild animals, 'a part of which had come from the land northward for food'.
detail: Two authors, about the same stretch of land, separated by many centuries of narrative, agree on the detail that animals moved south from the north.
Ether 9:31 even says this southern land was 'called by the Nephites Zarahemla', which agrees with Zarahemla being south.

tests.title: The scouts: did they think they had found Zarahemla?
tests.summary: Mosiah 8:8 says Limhi's scouts 'found not the land of Zarahemla'. Mosiah 21:26 says they found the bones land and, 'having supposed it to be the land of Zarahemla', went home.
detail: This is a location-belief inconsistency in how the two verses describe the same trip. It is reconcilable: they did not find Zarahemla, but believed the ruined land to be it, which is what Mosiah 21:26 says.
It also shows the scouts were lost, which fits Mosiah 21:25.

tests.title: Mormon-era retreat and treaty fit the earlier geography
tests.summary: The Nephites retreat north in stages, make a treaty giving them the land northward to the narrow passage, and then gather at Desolation by the pass.
detail: Mormon 2:3-6 retreats 'towards the north countries' through Angola, David and Joshua, which is in the borders west by the seashore. Mormon 2:20 reaches Shem 'northward'. Mormon 2:29 splits the land at the narrow passage: Nephites north, Lamanites south.
Mormon 3:5 then places city Desolation in the borders by that same pass, and Mormon 4:3 puts the city Teancum near it on the seashore. This agrees with Alma 22:30-32, 52:9 and 63:5.

tests.title: Hill Ramah (Jaredite) and Hill Cumorah (Nephite) are one hill
tests.summary: Ether 15:11 calls it the hill Ramah, 'that same hill where my father Mormon did hide up the records'. Mormon 6:6 says he hid them in the hill Cumorah. Both sit in the northern land of many waters.
detail: Ether 9:3 has Omer travel 'many days', pass the hill Shim, pass 'the place where the Nephites were destroyed', and go east to Ablom by the seashore. Mormon 1:3 quotes Ammaron saying the hill 'shall be called Shim', as if the name were still future, while Ether 9:3 (Moroni's abridgment) has Omer pass 'the hill of Shim' in Jaredite days. One reading is that Moroni uses the later name; the text does not say. It is a naming-time point, not a location conflict.

tests.title: Reused names for different places
tests.summary: Several names mean different places depending on the speaker and chapter. They are not contradictions, but they can look like them.
detail: Helaman 6:10 says the whole land south was called Lehi and the whole land north Mulek. Yet 'Lehi' is also a city on the Nephite east coast (Alma 50:15), and 'Mulek' is a city on that same coast just south of Bountiful (Alma 51:26), while the 'land called Mulek' is the whole land north of the neck.

'Jerusalem' is also a Lamanite city near the borders of Mormon (Alma 21:1-2). 'Bountiful' is both the land by the sea at the neck and the first stop by the sea in the Old World (1 Nephi 17:5). 'Gideon', 'Manti', 'Nephi', 'Moroni', 'Aaron', 'Noah', 'Teancum', 'Mormon' and 'Helam' are people as well as places.
